transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I can’t keep my mind on one thing. Like at work, I’m at the bench and I’ll be looking at a customer email, then I notice a saw mark on a piece, then there’s some noise outside, and suddenly I’ve completely lost track of the work order.

It’s frustrating because with jewelry, you know, tiny details matter—one little mistake and the whole piece is off. I used to be able to sit with something, but lately I’m just bouncing from one thing to another and not finishing what I’m supposed to be doing.
Do you find yourself getting distracted like this in other parts of your life, like at home or while driving, or is it mostly at work?

It’s… mostly what I notice at work, honestly. I mean, that’s where it really messes things up because I’m at the bench and I’ll start with a customer email, then my eye catches some saw mark on a piece, then there’s a noise outside, and next thing I know I’ve completely lost the work order.

At home I guess I get pulled off things too, but the reason I came in is the work stuff. Like, with jewelry, you can’t really afford to have your mind hopping around like that.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around a lot, even when you’re trying to focus on something?

Yeah, I do. At the bench especially, I can’t just sit there and stay with one thing. I’ll be sketching out a new watch case, then suddenly I’m up emailing suppliers, then I’m messing with the display trays like they have to be perfect right then.

And that’ll happen even after closing, which is stupid because nobody’s even there to see the trays, but I’ll still be moving around doing it instead of just finishing the one thing I meant to do.
Does this restlessness and need to move around happen even when you're at home, like when you're trying to relax or watch something?

Yeah… I mean, at home I’ll move around some, but the bigger thing is at work. Like I just can’t sit still at the bench. I’ll start sketching a new watch case, then I’m suddenly emailing suppliers, and then I’m over by the front rearranging display trays for no real reason.

And the weird part is I’ll keep doing that after closing too, when it doesn’t even matter because nobody’s there. I just keep bouncing around instead of staying put and finishing one thing.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized, upbeat, or irritable where you didn’t need much sleep and your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

Yeah… after the show, especially, I was kind of lit up. Like, larger than life almost, like everything I touched was going to turn into some big thing. And then if somebody was like, “Hey, can you just come in at normal hours,” or “maybe slow down a little,” I’d get really irritated fast.

It’s weird because one minute I felt amazing, like I could handle anything, and then the next I’d snap at people over normal shop stuff.
After those times when you felt unusually energized or irritable, did you ever experience a period where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for several days or more?

Yeah… yeah, after that kind of high wears off, it’s been the opposite. These past couple weeks especially, I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow feeling there, like the shine’s gone out of everything.

I mean, which sounds stupid coming from me because I’m literally around shiny things all day, stones and metal and all that, but… it’s like none of it catches me the same. I’ve sat in my truck before opening the shop and just cried for a bit before going in.

When your mind is racing or you're getting distracted, does that only happen during those times when you feel unusually energized or 'lit up,' or does it happen even when you're feeling more down or just normal too?

It’s… mostly when I’m kind of lit up, I think. That’s when it gets really obvious. Like what really made me come in was my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore.

At the bench, I’ll be trying to answer a customer email, and then I notice a saw mark on a piece, and then there’s some noise outside or in the front, and suddenly I’m looking up and realizing I’ve lost the whole work order. Then I have to start over and figure out what I was even doing.

I mean, the bench is already kind of chaotic sometimes—tiny stones, little parts everywhere, and if you drop one thing it’s like your whole day is gone—but this is different. It’s like my attention just jumps without asking me.
Do you ever find your mind racing or get really distracted even when you’re not feeling that ‘lit up’ or energized, like during times when you’re just feeling normal or even down?

I mean… yeah, I think so, but the worst of it is when I’m more revved up. What really brought me in is that my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore.

Like at the bench, I’ll start with a customer email, then I see a saw mark on a piece, then I hear something outside or up front, and suddenly I’m sitting there realizing I’ve completely lost the work order. And then I’m trying to piece together what I was even doing, which is… not great when you’ve got tiny parts everywhere.
Do you find your mind getting distracted and racing like this even when you’re not feeling either really high or really down—just kind of in your normal mood state?

I’m not totally sure I can separate it cleanly, honestly. Like, on a normal day I can get sidetracked some—my work kind of invites that, with all the little pieces and customers coming in and out—but what really made me think, okay, something’s off, is when my mind just wouldn’t stay on one thing.

I’ll be at the bench, start answering a customer email, then notice a saw mark on a piece, then hear some noise outside, and next thing I know I’ve lost the whole work order and I’m sitting there trying to reconstruct what I was doing. So… maybe a little when I’m normal, but the big noticeable version is that.
Can you think of a time when you weren’t feeling especially high or down, and your mind still raced or you found yourself getting distracted easily?

Maybe, yeah… it’s hard to pin down because at the shop everything is already kind of pulling at me. But the thing that really made me come in was that my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore.

Like I’ll be at the bench, and I’m supposed to answer a customer email, then I notice a saw mark on a piece I was working on, then there’s some noise outside or up front, and suddenly I’ve completely lost the work order. Then I’m sitting there trying to remember what I was even doing. It’s not like I just forgot where I put a tool—though that happens too, I mean, with little stones and parts everywhere—but this feels like my attention just jumps tracks.

Outside of work and outside of the times when you're feeling especially high or down, have you noticed problems with staying focused or getting easily distracted in other parts of your life, like when you're reading, watching something, or talking with someone?

Yeah, I mean… a little, but the clearest thing is still at work. Like, I’ll try to watch something at home and realize I missed half of it because I was thinking about some setting or a customer piece or—sorry, that’s work again.

It’s just, what really scared me was at the bench. My mind won’t stay put. I’ll go from a customer email to noticing a saw mark, then some noise outside pulls me, and then I look down and I’ve lost the whole work order. Then I’m sitting there with pieces out and I can’t remember what step I was on. That’s the part that feels really not like me.
Can you think of a time when you were not at work and not feeling especially high or down, where you still found it hard to focus or your mind wandered a lot?

I mean… not as clear, no. I keep coming back to the shop because that’s where it’s obvious. At home I can drift, but then I think, well, everybody does that, right? Like if the TV’s on and I’m thinking about something else.

What really brought me in is more like… at the bench, my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore. I’ll start with a customer email, then suddenly I’m looking at a saw mark, then some noise outside catches me, and then I realize I’ve lost the whole work order. That’s the part I can actually point to and say, okay, this isn’t normal for me.
Can you think of a time when you were not at work and not feeling especially high or down, where you still found it hard to focus or your mind wandered a lot?

I know you’re asking not at work, and I’m trying to think of one, but honestly I keep circling back to the bench because that’s where it feels real. Like, what brought me in is that my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore.

I’ll be answering a customer email, then I notice a saw mark, then some noise outside grabs me, and suddenly I’ve lost the whole work order. Then I’m just sitting there like… what was I doing? Outside of work, I don’t have as clean an example. It’s mostly that.
Can you think of a time when you were away from work, not feeling especially high or down, and still found it hard to focus or your mind kept jumping around a lot?

Away from work… I’m trying, but I honestly don’t have a great example. My brain keeps going right back to the bench, because that’s where it’s been obvious and kind of scary.

Like, I’ll be in the middle of a customer email, then I notice a saw mark, then a noise outside pulls me away, and next thing I know I’ve lost track of the whole work order. I’m sitting there with the pieces out like, wait, what step was I even on? That’s the thing that made me think something’s not right—my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore.
Can you think of a time when you were away from work, not feeling especially high or down, and still found it hard to focus or your mind kept jumping around a lot?

Away from work… I’m honestly having trouble landing on a clean example. Like, at home I’ll start watching something and then end up thinking about whether I left a tool out, or I’ll notice some little scratch on the table and get sidetracked, but it’s not as easy to point to.

The thing that really made me come in is still the bench. My mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore. I’ll be answering a customer email, then I’m staring at a saw mark, then some noise outside catches me, and suddenly I’ve lost the whole work order. Then I’m sitting there like, wait, where was I? That’s the part that feels not normal for me.
